text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: GPU pool eu-west-1 `gpu-pool-prod` reached 100% capacity and autoscaler failed to add nodes. Autoscaler reports repeated scale attempts and provider API 429/503s. Queue length spiked from 200 -> 450 in 10m. Alerting SLO breaches for latency and throttles. Paging oncall.
Sam (oncall): I'm on it. Acknowledge. Sam here. Any quick customer-impact signal?
Rob (CS): Seeing elevated errors from 3 paying customers in eu-west-1. Error rate up ~12% 5xx on inference endpoints and spike in queue retry counts. I've opened a troubleshooting ticket for CS.
Lee (infra): Looking at autoscaler logs now. Autoscaler attempted 4 scaleups in last 8m; each attempt hit provider rate limit or provisioning timeout. Last log lines: `scaleup attempt=4 desired=8 -> 12 reason=queue_growth` then `provider_err=429` then `backoff=30s`. Also node boot times prolonged (avg 240s).
Maya (ml-platform): Queue growth is mainly long-running text-generation jobs (seq len > 1024). We could temporarily force prefix caching eviction and reduce max_seq for the most expensive route to free up capacity. Also low-latency tier customers can be routed to eu-central fallback.
Nadia (infra): I can try a manual scale to get capacity up while we stabilize autoscaler. But provider API is flaky so manual might also fail. Proposing: 1) increase autoscaler.max_replicas to 30 temporarily; 2) set provider retry backoff to 10s; 3) do a manual `kubectl scale` if provider allows. Need thumbs.
Sam (oncall): Do it. Prioritize avoiding customer-facing errors. Put a note on status page that we're doing mitigations.
Lee (infra): Quick check: current autoscaler config: `min=4 max=12 targetUtil=0.7`. If we bump max->30, autoscaler will attempt more nodes but provider throttling might still block it. We should also enable cross-region fallback routing for non-SLA traffic.
Maya (ml-platform): I'll flip a routing rule to send non-enterprise requests from eu-west to eu-central for the next 30m. Patch snippet:
```
route_rules:
  - id: temp-eu-fallback
    match: region=="eu-west-1" and plan!=enterprise
    action: route_to eu-central-1
    ttl: 1800
```
I can push that in 2m.
Nadia (infra): Starting manual operations. Running:
```bash
# attempt manual scaleup
kubectl -n infra scale deployment/gpu-pool-prod --replicas=20
# bump autoscaler config
kubectl -n infra patch cm autoscaler-config -p '{"data":{"max_replicas":"30","provider_backoff":"10"}}'
```
Sam (oncall): Keep logs of any provider 429s and exact timestamps. I'll coordinate status updates. Rob, please prepare a short status message: "Partial impact to eu-west inference; mitigations in progress; routing and scaling attempted".
Rob (CS): Draft: "We're experiencing degraded inference performance for eu-west-1. We're adding capacity and routing non-enterprise traffic to eu-central. Enterprise customers unaffected where possible. Updates every 15m." Posting to status now.
Lee (infra): Manual scale command returned partial success: 6 nodes added, 2 failed due to provider timeouts. Autoscaler still logging provider 429s at 1748001270. Node boot times remain high. However queue length dropped from 450 -> 230 after first few nodes came up. Throttles decreased but still above SLO.
Maya (ml-platform): I pushed route rule. Non-enterprise traffic now flowing to eu-central. We're seeing immediate drop in request rate to eu-west for cheaper plans. This should reduce pressure on the pool.
Sam (oncall): Good. Next: can we temporarily evict long-running jobs older than 5m that are lower priority?
Maya (ml-platform): Yes. We have an eviction gate. Running prioritization: `prioritize=enterprise > realtime > batch`. I'll trigger eviction of `batch` jobs > 5m.
Nadia (infra): Eviction completed: reclaimed ~6 GPU-minutes, freed 4 queued slots. Combined with manual scale and routing, queue now ~120 and trending down. Throttles at ~2%.
Rob (CS): Customer impact update: error rates for affected tenants down from 12% -> 3%. CS team is notifying impacted customers with ETA for full recovery.
Sam (oncall): Nice work. We should still investigate root cause: why provider API started returning 429s and long boot times. Assigning follow-ups.
Lee (infra): Quick root hints: provider-side capacity exhaustion in the region, possibly provider-side maintenance or noisy tenant. Also our autoscaler backoff was conservative (exponential to 5m) which delayed retries. I'll capture metrics: provider_429_count, scale_attempts, node_boot_time.
Maya (ml-platform): Action items for immediate post-incident: 1) add routing playbook for cross-region fallback (Maya). 2) Add autoscaler safe-override to allow manual bump without waiting full backoff (Lee). 3) Create dashboard for queue length by region/model (Sam). 4) Explore per-tenant rate limiting to avoid noisy-neighbor effects (Product + CS) (Rob).
Sam (oncall): I'll create the incident ticket and assign owners. Tagging it P1 and linking logs. Handing off to night oncall in 40m. Night oncall, you'll have playbook in the ticket.
Rob (CS): I'll follow up with the 3 impacted customers and keep them updated.
Nadia (infra): For now I've reverted autoscaler.max_replicas->20 to avoid runaway costs, kept provider_backoff=10 for 30m, and left manual replicas=16. I'll document commands run in the ticket.
Sam (oncall): Closing live mitigation. Queue stable, errors within acceptable limits. We'll run a postmortem tomorrow 11:00 UTC. Please add any logs, times, and exact commands to the incident doc. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup: 
Maya (ml-platform): Added short note: consider implementing per-route max_seq enforcement during overload to reduce expensive jobs.
Lee (infra): I'll follow up with provider support to get root cause for 429s and request rate-limit exception if needed.
Sam (oncall): Handoff to night oncall: @Nadia (infra) will be primary for the next 4h. Sam out.
Nadia (infra): Acknowledged. Will monitor and escalate if queue > 300 or 5xx > 5%.
incident-bot: Incident marked as "mitigated" at 1748001450.
